description: Captures rows and ongoing row-level changes (insert/update/delete/truncate) from tables in a customer PostgreSQL database via logical replication, preceded by a watermark-fenced backfill of preexisting rows.

spec.sslPolicy: User-selectable advanced.sslmode (disable|allow|prefer|require|verify-ca|verify-full), validated against that exact list. When unset the connector adds no sslmode parameter at all, so libpq's own default applies; the sole exception is that sslmode=require is forced when auth_type is GCPIAM or AzureIAM and the user did not set sslmode explicitly. The DSN also always carries application_name=estuary_flow and lowered TCP keepalives (idle 120s, interval 30s, count 6) so half-open connections surface in ~5 minutes.
spec.tunnelSupport: Optional SSH bastion (networkTunnel.sshForwarding.sshEndpoint + privateKey). When set, a tunnel is started before any connection and the DSN host is rewritten to localhost:5432. Connection poolers are a hard config error: an address ending in '.pooler.supabase.com' or '.pooler.supabase.com:6543' is rejected as a user error because poolers silently ignore the replication=database option. Two separate connections are opened: a pgxpool for queries/backfill and a second pgconn with RuntimeParams["replication"]="database" for the replication stream.

artifacts: Logical replication slot, name from advanced.slotName (default 'flow_slot'), output plugin 'pgoutput'. Created by the connector over the replication protocol (CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT ... NOEXPORT_SNAPSHOT), but ONLY on the fresh-start path (empty resume cursor) and only while the default 'create_replication_slot' feature flag is on; that same path drops the slot first. Pins restart_lsn.

Publication, name from advanced.publicationName (default 'flow_publication'). NOT created by the connector: prerequisitePublication counts pg_catalog.pg_publication rows and hard-fails with 'publication %q does not exist' if absent (the README's claim that the connector will attempt to create one is stale relative to the code). The connector DOES mutate it: addTableToPublication issues 'ALTER PUBLICATION ... ADD TABLE' for every captured table not already published, and for the watermarks table.

Watermarks table, name from advanced.watermarksTable (default 'public.flow_watermarks'), schema (slot TEXT PRIMARY KEY, watermark TEXT). Auto-created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS when permissions allow, and itself added to the publication. It does not grow: writes are an upsert of a single row keyed by the slot name. Skipped entirely under advanced.read_only_capture.
continuity.customerSideAccrual: WAL on the customer's primary. PostgreSQL will not recycle any WAL segment newer than the slot's restart_lsn, and restart_lsn only advances while the connector is CONNECTED: a background goroutine sends a Standby Status Update every 10s carrying ackLSN, which Acknowledge() sets from Flow's own durable checkpoint. Between runs no status update is sent at all, so every byte of WAL generated by the whole database (not just captured tables) from the last acknowledged LSN onward is retained on the customer's disk for the entire gap. An abandoned or chronically lagging slot grows pg_wal without bound until the disk fills and the database goes read-only — unless the operator has set max_slot_wal_keep_size, in which case the server invalidates the slot instead (see ourSideLoss). Secondary, much smaller accrual: one upserted row in the watermarks table, plus the WAL those writes themselves generate (the watermarks table is in the publication).
continuity.ourSideLoss: Slot invalidation. If the server bounds retention via max_slot_wal_keep_size, an over-retained slot is invalidated and pg_replication_slots.wal_status becomes 'lost'. The connector detects this at stream startup but only emits a WARNING — 'replication slot was invalidated by the server, it must be deleted and all bindings backfilled' — and proceeds. So the loss is not a clean failure: it is a full re-backfill of every binding, and until a human acts on that log line the capture keeps running from a hole in the WAL. The same warning-only treatment applies when the slot is already active (another capture running), when confirmed_flush_lsn is null, and when the resume LSN is behind confirmed_flush_lsn (the signature of a dropped-and-recreated slot). Separately, losing the resume cursor is destructive rather than merely a restart: an empty start cursor drops and recreates the slot, discarding retained WAL and forcing every binding to re-backfill.
continuity.resumeWindow: Not bounded by the connector — there is no lease, TTL, or expiry on its side, and nothing in the code limits how long it may stay disconnected. The window is set entirely by the customer's server configuration: unbounded (retention grows until pg_wal fills the disk) when max_slot_wal_keep_size is unset, which is the PostgreSQL default; otherwise however long it takes that database's write volume to produce max_slot_wal_keep_size of WAL past restart_lsn, after which the slot is invalidated. The connector never reads or sets max_slot_wal_keep_size, so this window is not observable from the connector config.
continuity.notes: CONFIRMED: the slot is never dropped on shutdown. replicationStream.Close() cancels the standby-status goroutine, waits for it, and closes the socket with a termination message — nothing else. The only DropReplicationSlot call in the connector is inside recreateReplicationSlot, reached only from the fresh-start (empty cursor) branch of ReplicationStream. So after every run — clean exit, crash, or a cron tick simply ending — 'flow_slot' remains on the customer's database with active=false, still pinning restart_lsn. VERDICT FOR A 45-SECOND SERVERLESS CRON TICK: unsafe as a design. This is a log-mode connector whose safety model assumes a long-lived process; ReplicationPollingInterval() returns 0 precisely because events arrive continuously rather than being polled for. Under a short-tick cron the slot spends nearly all wall-clock time inactive-but-retaining, WAL retention on the customer's primary is driven by the interval between ticks rather than by anything we control, and any tick that fails to durably checkpoint leaves restart_lsn exactly where it was so the next tick inherits the backlog. Startup cost per tick is also non-trivial and partly write-side: prerequisite checks re-run (SHOW wal_level, role check, slot/publication lookups, a watermarks-table existence write of the literal string 'existence-check', and an ALTER PUBLICATION check per table), two connections are opened, and StreamToFence writes a fresh watermark UUID on every fence — during ongoing streaming as well as during backfill, not just per backfill chunk. The connector does watch for the failure modes it cannot prevent (PeriodicChecks warns on transactions open >30 min and on a restart_lsn/confirmed_flush_lsn gap over 4GB) but only by logging. Mitigation if short ticks are unavoidable: advanced.read_only_capture removes the watermark writes (with documented correctness tradeoffs), but it does nothing about slot retention, which is the actual hazard.

configFields.name: user

configFields.name: historyMode

configFields.name: credentials.aws_session_token
configFields.description: Session credential injected by the control plane; required at runtime for AWSIAM.

configFields.name: credentials.azure_access_token

configFields.name: discoveryFilters.include_schemas
configFields.description: Array of schemas; when non-empty only tables in these schemas are discovered. Unioned with advanced.discover_schemas and pushed into the listing query.

configFields.name: discoveryFilters.exclude_schemas
configFields.description: Array of schemas excluded from discovery, applied client-side after listing.

configFields.name: discoveryFilters.table_patterns
configFields.description: Array of glob patterns ('*'/'?'); a pattern containing '.' matches the qualified schema.table, otherwise the unqualified table name in any schema. Validated at config time via tableglob.Compile.

configFields.name: discoveryFilters.discover_unpublished_tables
configFields.description: Discover tables not currently in the publication; unioned with the identically-named advanced option. Such tables are added to the publication at capture time if permissions allow.

configFields.name: advanced.publicationName
configFields.description: PostgreSQL publication to replicate from. Default flow_publication. Must already exist — the connector will not create it.

configFields.name: advanced.slotName
configFields.description: PostgreSQL replication slot name. Default flow_slot. Created by the connector on a fresh start if absent.

configFields.name: advanced.watermarksTable
configFields.description: Fully-qualified '<schema>.<table>' used for watermark writes. Default public.flow_watermarks. Config validation rejects a name without a period.

configFields.name: advanced.skip_backfills
configFields.description: Comma-separated fully-qualified table names not to backfill; the literal '*.*' skips all backfills. Each entry must contain a period.

configFields.name: advanced.backfill_chunk_size
configFields.description: Rows fetched per backfill query. Default 50000.

configFields.name: advanced.sslmode
configFields.description: Overrides the libpq sslmode parameter. Enum: disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca, verify-full.

configFields.name: advanced.discover_schemas
configFields.description: Array; when non-empty only these schemas are discovered, pushed into the table-listing query as 'nspname = ANY($n)'. Blank entries are a validation error.

configFields.name: advanced.min_backfill_xid
configFields.description: Digits only. Backfill only rows whose xmin exceeds this XID under 32-bit modular comparison; a 0.1% random sample is always included so data keeps trickling through fully-excluded regions.

configFields.name: advanced.read_only_capture
configFields.description: Operate without watermark writes; skips both watermarks-table prerequisites, with documented correctness tradeoffs.

configFields.name: advanced.capture_as_partitions
configFields.description: Discover partition leaves individually rather than the root table. Requires a publication created without publish_via_partition_root.

configFields.name: advanced.discover_unpublished_tables
configFields.description: Same as the discoveryFilters option; the two are ORed together.

configFields.name: advanced.source_tag
configFields.description: Emitted as the 'tag' property in each document's source metadata; the property is removed from the schema entirely when unset.

configFields.name: advanced.rediscovery_interval
configFields.description: Duration string matching ^[0-9]+(ms|s|m|h)$; how often discovery re-runs while a capture is live to notice schema changes and new tables. Default 15m.

configFields.name: advanced.statement_timeout
configFields.description: Overrides the connector's statement_timeout (SET per connection). Blank uses the 2-minute default; '0' disables timeouts. Enum: '', 0, 30s, 1m, 2m, 5m, 30m.

configFields.name: advanced.feature_flags
configFields.description: Estuary-internal comma-separated flags. Defaults on: use_schema_inference, emit_sourced_schemas, date_as_date, time_as_time, flatten_arrays, create_replication_slot. Defaults off: multidimensional_arrays, skip_prerequisites, skip_table_prerequisites. Also accepts value-carrying flags initial_backfill_cursor=<lsn> and force_reset_cursor=<lsn>.

configFields.name: advanced.discover_only_published
configFields.description: Hidden and unused; retained only so existing captures do not break.

configFields.name: networkTunnel.sshForwarding.sshEndpoint
configFields.description: ssh://user@hostname[:port] bastion used to tunnel to the database; enforced by pattern ^ssh://.+@.+$.

configFields.name: networkTunnel.sshForwarding.privateKey
configFields.description: Multiline private key for the SSH bastion.

discovery.method: pg_catalog system-catalog queries: a table listing from pg_class joined to pg_namespace, then chunked (100 tables at a time) per-table column/type, primary-key, unique-secondary-index, generated-column and column-comment queries; publication membership from pg_publication_tables.
discovery.querySketch: Listing: select namespace name and relation name from pg_class joined to pg_namespace, where nspname is not one of the excluded system schemas, relpersistence='p' (excluding temporary and unlogged), and either (default) NOT relispartition AND relkind IN ('r','p'), or (capture_as_partitions) relkind='r'; an optional 'nspname = ANY($1)' clause pushes the selected-schemas list into the query. Columns: pg_attribute joined to pg_type/pg_class/pg_namespace with a (schema, table) row-constructor IN-clause, ordered by attnum. Primary keys: pg_index where indisprimary, expanded via information_schema._pg_expandarray to recover key ordering (adapted from pgjdbc getPrimaryKeys). Fallback keys: pg_index where indisunique AND indexprs IS NULL AND relkind='r'. Column descriptions via information_schema.columns with col_description(). Slot state from pg_catalog.pg_replication_slots, including a row_to_json/COALESCE trick to read wal_status only when the column exists (PG13+).
excludes: schemas pg_catalog, pg_internal, information_schema, catalog_history, cron, pglogical
partition leaves (relispartition) unless capture_as_partitions is set
partitioned root tables (relkind='p') when capture_as_partitions is set
tables not matching any discoveryFilters.table_patterns glob when patterns are supplied
tables absent from the configured publication unless discover_unpublished_tables is set (either the advanced or discoveryFilters copy)

authTierRationale: The default and easiest path is a host/user/password DSN: no OAuth app registration and no refresh token. The three IAM variants are also T1 in credential terms — the user supplies only non-secret identifiers (region + role ARN, service account + audience, or client id + tenant id) and the actual short-lived session credentials are injected by the Flow control plane rather than typed in — so they add no user-side app registration either. The real cost of this connector is DBA work, not credential work: wal_level=logical (which requires a database restart), a role with the REPLICATION attribute, a pre-existing publication, and write access for the watermarks table. That is not what the tier scale measures, but a downstream reader should not read T1_SIMPLE as 'self-serve in two minutes'.

unionMisfits.description: Every stream is discovered from the customer's catalog, so no literal stream list exists in the source; the per-stream facts are uniform across all discovered tables and are given here as a template rather than fabricated names. Each table has exactly the two pull shapes v2 introduced: a watermark-fenced keyset/TID backfill and a shared pgoutput streaming leg. The only literal table the connector names is the watermarks table, which is a control artifact it writes to, not a capture stream.

proposedShape.name: <schema>.<table> (discovered)
proposedShape.primaryKey: table PRIMARY KEY columns in key order; falls back to a unique non-expression secondary index on an ordinary table; final fallback collection key for keyless tables is ['/_meta/source/loc/0','/_meta/source/loc/1','/_meta/source/loc/2'] (WAL location)
proposedShape.primaryKeyKind: columns (synthetic json_pointers into WAL location for keyless tables)

backfill.querySketch: Keyed: SELECT * FROM "<schema>"."<table>" [WHERE (key tuple) > (previous chunk's last key tuple)] ORDER BY <key columns> LIMIT <backfill_chunk_size, default 50000>. Text-ish key columns (varchar/bpchar/text) get COLLATE "C" in both the comparison and the ORDER BY when a precise backfill is requested, so ordering is bytewise. Keyless: SELECT * FROM "<schema>"."<table>" WHERE ctid > $1 AND ctid <= $2 (TID range scan; the connector also disables parallel workers per connection so the planner does not turn this into a full scan). When min_backfill_xid is set, 'xmin::text AS xmin' is prepended to the projection and a modular-XID predicate ANDed in, plus a RANDOM() < 0.001 escape so excluded regions still trickle.
backfill.chunking: One chunk per query, bounded by LIMIT backfill_chunk_size (keyed) or by the ctid range (keyless), and fenced by a watermark write: write a watermark UUID, stream replication events until that write is observed while patching changes falling inside the buffered chunk, emit the buffered chunk, then issue the next chunk query.

incremental.resumeTokenKind: PostgreSQL LSN — a single stream-wide value (pglogrepl.LSN, checkpointed as a JSON string), not per-table. START_REPLICATION SLOT <slot> LOGICAL <lsn> ("proto_version" '1', "publication_names" '<pub>'). All bindings share one slot and one WAL stream, which is why scope is 'database' rather than 'table'.

unionMisfits.description: Both fields are single strings, but the accrual here is conditional on a customer-side setting the connector cannot observe: with max_slot_wal_keep_size unset (the PostgreSQL default) the customer accrues unbounded WAL and we lose nothing; with it set, the customer accrues at most that much and WE lose the slot to invalidation and owe a full re-backfill. It is one mechanism with two mutually exclusive outcomes selected by a server GUC, not two independent risks, and a reader deciding cron-tick safety needs to see the branch.

accrualBranches.customerSideAccrual: unbounded pg_wal growth until disk exhaustion

accrualBranches.ourSideLoss: slot invalidated (wal_status='lost'); warning only; every binding must be re-backfilled

unionMisfits.description: artifacts is a list of strings, which flattens away the three properties that actually decide risk: who created the artifact, whether the connector ever removes it, and whether it is written to during steady-state operation. Those differ per artifact here — the slot is created and (only on cursor reset) dropped by us, the publication is created by the user but mutated by us, and the watermarks table is created and written by us but does not grow.

artifacts.name: flow_slot
artifacts.droppedByConnector: only on the fresh-start / empty-cursor path

artifacts.name: flow_publication
artifacts.mutatedByConnector: ALTER PUBLICATION ... ADD TABLE per captured table and for the watermarks table

artifacts.name: public.flow_watermarks
artifacts.writtenDuringSteadyState: one row upserted per StreamToFence, i.e. during ongoing streaming as well as backfill, unless read_only_capture

unionMisfits.description: The three-value tier scale measures user effort in registering an app or obtaining a token, and rates all four modes here T1. It has no way to express that this connector's dominant setup cost is database administration performed out-of-band: ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_level=logical plus a database restart, CREATE USER ... REPLICATION, GRANT pg_read_all_data, and CREATE PUBLICATION. A connector-selection UI driven by tier alone will present this as being as easy as pasting an API key.

steps: ALTER SYSTEM SET wal_level = logical (+ restart)
GRANT pg_read_all_data (or per-schema SELECT + default privileges)
CREATE PUBLICATION flow_publication FOR ALL TABLES
grant write access for the watermarks table unless read_only_capture

abstained.streams: Fully discovered from the customer's catalog; the connector names no capture streams at all. The only literal table name in the source is the control-plane watermarks table (public.flow_watermarks), which is written to rather than captured, so listing it as a stream would be wrong. Per-stream facts are recorded in unionMisfits[0].proposedShape instead, per schema rule 7.
abstained.streams[].cursorField: There is no per-table cursor column. The resume cursor is one stream-wide WAL LSN (pglogrepl.ParseLSN, checkpointed as a JSON string) shared by the whole capture. Backfill chunk resumption separately uses the primary-key tuple, or ctid for keyless tables, but neither is a cursorField in the schema's sense.
abstained.execution.schedule: Recorded as 'continuous' because ReplicationPollingInterval() returns 0 with the comment that logical replication events arrive continuously rather than being polled for, and the connector streams until a fence. But the actual cadence is set by the 'fenceAfter' duration the Flow runtime passes into StreamToFence, which is not visible in this connector directory, so 'continuous' describes the connector's own model rather than a scheduling guarantee.
abstained.execution.continuity.resumeWindow: Recorded qualitatively rather than as a duration. The bound is max_slot_wal_keep_size on the customer's server divided by their WAL write rate; the connector never reads or sets that GUC — it only observes the resulting wal_status='lost' after the fact — so no numeric window can be derived from this source.
abstained.streams[].writeDisposition: Inferred, not read. Change events carry op codes (c/u/d) and a row key, implying merge/upsert downstream, and historyMode is documented as 'capture change events without reducing them to a final state', implying append. The reduction itself happens in the Flow runtime outside this connector directory.
abstained.credentialModes[1..3].tier: Rated T1_SIMPLE on the grounds that the user supplies only non-secret identifiers and the Flow control plane injects the session credentials (the AWSTokens/GCPTokens/AzureTokens fields are json-omitempty with no jsonschema titles, i.e. not user-facing). The control-plane code that populates them is outside this repository, so the claim that the user never supplies them is inferred from the schema shape rather than read directly. Standalone — without that control plane — AWSIAM would require the user to supply access key, secret, and session token themselves.
abstained.configFields.required: Requiredness is derived from struct tags ('omitempty' marks a field non-required per the SetDefaults comment) plus the explicit checks in Config.Validate and IAMConfig.ValidateIAM. The rendered JSON schema's own required[] array is produced by schemagen at build time and was not evaluated, so per-field requiredness for the oneOf branches is a reading of the validators rather than of the emitted schema.
